title: Umbraflow ProjectRegistrationManifest v3
$comment: The two-closure registration. A generation carries a reducer closure compiled on the pure program type and a tool closure compiled on the scoped program type, each with its own module manifest hash and its own stated export surface. There is ONE reader and it accepts project_registration_format 6 and refuses everything else, so the format integer is an identity assertion inside a reader and never a key anything dispatches on. Format 6 is format 5 without project_observation_schema_hash and reconcile_payload_schema_manifest_hash: derive and reconcile were the only judges of the documents those two pinned, and a pinned document nothing judges is the defect.

project_registration_format.$comment: The generation of this registration contract a framework must understand, not the bytes of the file that states it. Editing this schema's prose is not a new generation and must not move the registration root of a project already published against it.

reducer_closure.$comment: The closure compiled on the pure program type. Its exported_entry_points is exactly ["reduce"]: the pure type keeps one entry, and derive, plan, next_step and reconcile died with the five-function contract the Tool Runtime replaces. The slot is required, and there is deliberately no reading in which an absent reducer closure means a project that does not fold.

tool_closure.$comment: The closure compiled on the scoped program type. Its exported_entry_points is exactly the union of project_tool_bindings' entry points. The slot is required and stays required: a project that binds no Tool ships this closure with an empty exported_entry_points and an empty project_tool_bindings, because explicit emptiness is a value and an optional slot would be an absent-means-pure reading. Re-introducing the optional form to spare pure projects one empty array is the change this comment exists to refuse.

observed_instance_identity_schema_hashes.$comment: The closed set of observed-instance identity schema documents this registration owns, as the sha256 of each exact document. The deployment names the documents and the loader derives every digest from the bytes it read, sorted and unique by that derivation -- JSON Schema cannot state sortedness, so the framework's own reading of the derived document refuses any other order.

project_resources.$comment: One resource closure per registration, read by both closures. A registration pins the bytes a project registered once, so two program types loading two resource closures would be two answers to which bytes this project registered, and only one of them would be inside project_registration_hash.

project_tool_bindings.$comment: The Project Tool binding table: one row per Tool this registration binds to an entry point of the tool closure. It sits beside tool_catalog_hash rather than inside the catalog because a binding is the join of a contract name and a code entry, and a catalog carrying it could no longer be served to a caller and verified against the pinned digest. It is inside this root because a re-registration that rebound a Tool to different code without moving project_registration_hash would leave the pinned environment no longer pinning which code answers a call. Sorted and unique by tool_name -- JSON Schema cannot state sortedness, so the framework's own reading refuses any other order. An empty array is a registration that binds no Tool.

closure.$comment: One compiled closure of a generation. Both members are required in every version of this contract: exported_entry_points is what the authoring path observed the closure to offer, and a version of this schema without it would teach a reader that an absent statement means an unchecked one -- the exact absent-means-something reading the join exists to refuse. The declaration is the entry points only; plugin_id is a field of every closure and is never named here, so an empty array is the whole statement that a closure offers no entry point.
